text: Contributing Use Python 3.10–3.14 and Poetry 2: poetry install poetry run pre-commit install poetry run makim all.ci poetry check --lock Update dependencies using poetry lock , never by editing the lockfile. Frontend preference checks use Node 24 without npm dependencies: node tests/theme.cjs src/doukimd/themes/default/theme.js . CI runs them separately; pytest also runs them when Node is installed. Douki docstrings must be synchronized and idempotent: poetry run douki sync src tests examples/basic/src poetry run douki check src tests examples/basic/src The Makim groups, hooks, and release configuration are adapted from Douki , commit f77adee49546d4ea8e95ced671d470379c5bd741 . The BSD license and upstream attribution are retained. Documentation is built with DoukiMD. Publication is never triggered by pull requests. Publish the documentation After merging documentation changes, run the Documentation workflow manually from upstream main . It builds the site and publishes the documentation artifact to the gh-pages branch. Push and pull-request runs only build and validate the documentation. After the first manual run creates gh-pages , configure Settings → Pages to Deploy from a branch , selecting gh-pages and / (root) . The publishing action adds .nojekyll for the generated static site.

text: Authoring and configuration Run doukimd build --config doukimd.yaml or doukimd check . The latter compiles and validates without writing output. Paths are relative to the configuration file; directory traversal and paths escaping the project are rejected. See the runnable project under examples/basic . Markdown and metadata Markdown and .ipynb pages under docs/ become HTML at the same relative path. Optional YAML front matter accepts title , render ( markdown or jinja ), and meta , plus the page controls described below. Unknown keys, duplicate keys, invalid types, and malformed YAML are errors. Enable Jinja with render: jinja . Templates receive site , project , page , data , api , plugins , and build . Project configuration and front matter remain literal YAML. Content is rendered once, before Markdown parsing. Values returned by templates are not evaluated again. Content includes come from includes/ . Use the md_text filter when inserting a plain string into Markdown. Jinja syntax inside code fences is still evaluated on templated pages: use Jinja raw blocks for literal examples. Docstring prose is parsed as Markdown and never evaluated as Jinja. The dialect includes CommonMark, tables, footnotes, API blocks, and API references. Raw HTML is disabled by default. Python code highlighting uses Pygments; unknown languages fall back to plain text. Configuration Required settings are site.title and project.name . Defaults are schema_version: 1 , docs_dir: docs , output_dir: build , and includes_dir: includes . Data is a mapping of names to YAML mapping files. project.version is optional. api.generate_pages defaults to true. An API source has language: python , a project-relative root , and modules containing import paths. Configured modules and their declared submodules, classes, and functions are collected statically. Included public declarations require valid Douki docstrings. Explicit Douki visibility and atpublic decorators control visibility; underscores do not imply privacy. Literal __all__ selects exported declarations; package submodules are also collected. Without __all__ , local declarations are included, while imports are followed only when explicitly exported. Unresolved or cyclic exports fail the build. Re-exports retain their public names and original declaration identity and location. Exported aliases must resolve within the selected source folder; runtime inspection and external dependency imports are disabled. Properties, enum values, fields, constants, and annotated type aliases have reference pages. Data declarations can rely on their source annotations and values without an invented docstring; class field descriptions are reused from Douki attributes . Handwritten modules, classes, and callables still require valid Douki documentation. Generated dataclass constructors are identified as generated and use their statically derived signatures. Plum dispatch families (including aliases and Base.method.dispatch registrations) retain every signature and its own docstring. Typing overloads retain their declared signatures and use implementation prose when a stub has no docstring. Unknown repeated-definition patterns fail instead of retaining only the last declaration. Inherited members are not expanded in this version. Selecting source folders per page Name sources to isolate packages in a monorepo: api: sources: - name: arx root: packages/arx/src - name: irx root: packages/irx/src When modules is omitted, DoukiMD discovers top-level Python modules and regular packages in the folder. The folder can also be a package directory containing __init__.py . Set modules: [irx.table_io] to select a smaller surface from a source tree. Namespace packages remain unsupported. Select a default source for a Markdown page: --- title: IRx reference api_source: irx --- ::: api irx.table_io members: public ::: See {@api irx.table_io}. An individual API block can override the page choice with source: arx . Fully qualified references such as {@api python:arx:arx.get_version} can link across sources. Ambiguous unscoped names and unknown source names fail the build. Folder paths are configured once; Markdown uses source names. Two folders may contain identically named Python packages without collisions. Duplicate source names are errors. Named sources use identities python:<source>:<qualified-name> and routes api/python/<source>/<qualified-name>.html . Unnamed sources retain the original python:<qualified-name> identities and routes. The symbol inventory includes source_name , original canonical identity, generated , and callable variants with signatures and declaration lines. When API names collide on a case-insensitive filesystem (such as a public Compiler class and a compiler module), their filenames receive stable identity-derived suffixes. API references and generated summaries use the planned routes automatically. API blocks and references ::: api python:example.add show_source: true ::: API blocks accept members: none or members: public and boolean show_source . The latter displays a source location, not a repository link. {@api python:example.add} links to the canonical generated page. Unknown symbols and references without a generated destination fail the build. Generated pages live at api/python/<qualified-name>.html . Duplicate routes are errors; authored overrides and canonical aliases are not implemented. API directives inside docstrings are rejected. When collected symbols exist and api.generate_pages is enabled, the engine also generates api/index.html (served at /api/ ). The menu gathers all references under API Docs , with nested modules, classes, and functions. The index lists root declarations; each reference page summarizes and links to its immediate children. Explicitly selected submodules remain visible even when their parent module is outside the configured collection. The default menu is automatic; explicit project menus can place or scope API entries as described below. The bundled theme expands the active API branch and lists section anchors under On this page . Disabling generated pages removes the API section. Project navigation Without navigation settings, every authored page and the generated API tree appear in the sidebar. Explicit menus preserve your configured order: navigation: navbar: - title: Home path: index.md - title: Arx path: arx/index.md - title: Tools children: - title: Repository url: https://github.com/arxlang/arx default_sidebar: project sidebars: - id: project title: ArxLang items: - title: Home path: index.md - title: API Docs api: "*" - id: arx title: Arx paths: [arx/, api/python/arx/] items: - title: Overview path: arx/index.md - title: Language children: - title: Getting started path: arx/getting-started.md - title: Python API api: arx path is relative to the documentation root and accepts Markdown or HTML page names, directory URLs, queries, and heading anchors. The engine checks these targets and computes links relative to each output page. url accepts HTTP, HTTPS, or mailto links. A children group needs no target; a page or external link may also have children. api: "*" inserts the complete generated API tree. api: arx selects only symbols from the source named arx in api.sources ; no filesystem paths or handwritten API routes are needed in the menu. A single package links to its root page; multiple roots form a collapsible group. API generation must be enabled and the selected source must have generated pages. A sidebar's paths match output route prefixes ending in / , or exact HTML routes. The longest matching prefix wins; equally specific matches across sidebars are errors. Set sidebar: arx in front matter to select a menu explicitly, or sidebar: false to hide it. Otherwise the configured default_sidebar applies. With explicit sidebars and no default, unmatched pages have no sidebar. All configured menu targets are checked, including menus that are currently hidden. Index links for a product directory mark that product's navbar branch active on its descendants. Page layouts and branding Front matter supports layout: docs (the default), full (unrestricted site width), or landing (full width without the sidebar, title banner, or TOC). Use boolean toc , show_title , and sidebar to control the standard layout. A page's first Markdown heading remains authored content; show_title: false hides only the theme banner. site: title: ArxLang description: Compiler ecosystem documentation logo: images/arx-logo.png logo_alt: ArxLang favicon: favicon.ico assets: [assets/**, images/**, favicon.ico, styles.css] theme: stylesheets: [styles.css] Assets and stylesheet paths are relative to docs_dir . Patterns select files or directories recursively; nondefault patterns that match nothing are errors. Markdown and notebooks are document inputs and cannot be copied as assets. Asset paths cannot escape the documentation directory, and output collisions with pages, theme files, metadata, or differently cased filenames fail before publication. Logos, favicons, and extra stylesheets must be copied assets; the engine computes their URLs for nested pages. CSS is copied unchanged; use URLs relative to its output location. SCSS compilation is not included. An explicit assets list replaces the default, so keep assets/** when needed. For custom homepage markup, opt in with html: true in front matter. Combine it with render: jinja to use metadata in HTML or Markdown. This is trusted authored HTML, without sanitization; enable it only for content you control. Douki docstrings keep HTML escaped independently of the page setting. CommonMark requires blank lines around HTML wrappers to parse Markdown inside. HTML id anchors participate in link validation; duplicate ids fail. Local HTML href , src , and poster attributes are checked and Markdown page links rewritten, just like ordinary Markdown links. CSS URLs, srcset , inline scripts, and custom-template links are outside this validation. A page can choose template: home.html from theme.directory . To customize part of the bundled layout, that template can extend page.html and override Jinja blocks head , header , page_heading , page_content , or footer . For example, {% extends "page.html" %} followed by {% block footer %}<footer>ArxLang</footer>{% endblock %} changes the footer. Missing templates or template paths escaping their configured root fail. Links and output Relative Markdown links are rewritten to HTML and checked after all pages and heading anchors are known. Duplicate heading anchors get stable numeric suffixes. Local images and downloads must match the configured assets patterns (by default docs/assets/** ). External and site-root links are not fetched or checked. Output includes HTML, CSS, the local search script and index, symbols.json , and a versioned build manifest. No generated Markdown is written into source. DoukiMD replaces an existing output directory only when its manifest identifies it as a managed build. A failed compilation preserves the previous output. The output directory must not overlap documentation, source, includes, theme, or configured data inputs. Notebooks Version 4 Jupyter notebooks are discovered alongside Markdown. A notebook tutorials/lesson.ipynb produces tutorials/lesson.html ; links and menus can use the .ipynb name, including queries and heading anchors. Notebook and Markdown files share one route namespace, so matching stems are errors. Builds validate the original document against nbformat's shipped schema and render existing cells and outputs. They never start a kernel, import notebook code, install its dependencies, execute cells, or change notebook files. Run notebooks in Jupyter separately to refresh their saved results. The first cell, when Markdown, can contain the same YAML front matter as a .md page. Alternatively, put page settings in notebook JSON metadata under metadata.doukimd ; first-cell front matter overrides explicitly supplied fields. All page controls, API source selection, and search exclusion apply. With render: jinja , only Markdown cell sources are templated. Code, raw cells, attachments, and saved outputs remain literal. Markdown cells support the normal API blocks, references, local links, headings, and TOC. Reference definitions and footnotes are scoped to their cell; footnotes receive unique page-wide ids. Code is highlighted using language_info.name or kernelspec.language . Raw cells render as escaped text. Standard cell tags remove-cell , remove-input , and remove-output omit the selected content from both HTML and search; the latter two apply to code cells. Saved stdout, stderr, and tracebacks render as escaped text without ANSI control codes. MIME bundles choose one representation in this order: HTML, SVG, PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, Markdown, JSON, then plain text. Markdown outputs use plain CommonMark and tables without Jinja or API directives. Unsupported formats need a supported fallback; otherwise the build fails with a cell location. A widget with a plain-text fallback displays that fallback. PNG and other raster outputs are validated as base64. Images and Markdown image attachments are embedded as data URLs, with SVG kept in image context. HTML outputs use sandboxed frames with scripts, forms, parent access, and external resource loading disabled. Inline styles and embedded data images are allowed; frames can be resized vertically. Interactive widgets and JavaScript outputs are not executed. Rich-output links are separate from document reference validation. Try doukimd build --config examples/notebooks/doukimd.yaml for a complete example with saved output. Local search Search is enabled by default and runs in the reader's browser, using only the bundled search.js and lazily fetched search.json . It indexes guide prose, code, generated API documentation, and visible notebook content, with links to Markdown heading anchors. API result titles include qualified identities. Each query requires all its words; title matches rank above body matches, and results keep the best matching section per page. search: enabled: true limit: 8 min_length: 2 limit accepts 1–50 results; min_length accepts 1–10 characters. Set search: false in page front matter or notebook page metadata to omit that page from the index. This affects search, not whether the page is published. Disabling the site search omits its controls, script, and index. Open search with the header button, / , or Ctrl/Cmd+K when outside editable controls. Arrow keys move between results, Tab follows native dialog focus, and Escape closes the dialog and restores focus. Queries support Unicode normalization and case-insensitive matching. Failed index loads show a retry message. Result text is inserted as text, never interpreted as HTML. Serve the generated site over HTTP, including under a repository subpath. For local use: python -m http.server --directory build . Browsers generally block fetching the search index when opening HTML through file:// . Search requires JavaScript and native dialog support; other navigation works without either. Custom themes receive search , search_script , and search_index_url to integrate their own controls. The index is a JSON array of {title, url, text} records, with site-root-relative page and section URLs. Themes and plugins The bundled theme uses Bootstrap by default. Configure presentation under theme : theme: framework: bootstrap color_mode: auto palette: terracotta framework accepts bootstrap or none ; the latter omits Bootstrap for custom themes. Bootstrap 5.3.8 CSS and its license are bundled locally. Builds and readers do not need a CDN, npm, or Bootstrap JavaScript. The built-in layout and appearance controls also work with none . color_mode accepts auto (the system preference), light , or dark . Readers can change Appearance in the header; their choice overrides the configured default and is saved per project when browser storage is available. System mode follows subsequent OS preference changes. Without JavaScript, the configured light/dark mode is used; auto falls back to light. Navigation stays usable without JavaScript, including on mobile. palette accepts five presets: terracotta (the default), ocean , forest , violet , and slate . Each has light and dark colors and works with either framework setting. Readers can change Palette in the header independently of Appearance; both choices persist per project when storage is available. Invalid saved values fall back to configuration. Without JavaScript, the configured palette still applies. Light and dark colors for all five presets Select the chart to open it at full size. It shows all nine theme color roles in both modes, using the exact preset values. Terracotta keeps DoukiMD's original colors. The other four presets use Radix Colors 3.0.0 scales under the MIT license, bundled with their attribution. They require no Radix components, npm package, or network access. Body text, muted text, links, and active navigation colors are checked at 4.5:1 or better against their backgrounds. API-kind colors stay consistent across palettes. API labels identify modules, classes, functions, and methods in navigation and declaration headings. Method kinds are collected from class parentage, including static and class methods. Labels use text as well as color. Set theme.directory to a local directory containing page.html to override the bundled HTML template. Themes receive the content context plus content , navigation (the selected sidebar), navbar , sidebar_title , table_of_contents , and stylesheet . Navigation entries expose title , relative url , kind (null for authored pages), current (exact route), active (current route or descendant), and recursive children . Group-only entries have a null url ; render their labels without an anchor. Table-of-contents entries expose title , anchor url , and level ( h2 or h3 ). Both structures are planned by the engine and can be styled by themes. HTML autoescaping is enabled; only the engine-rendered content should use Jinja's safe filter. Templates also receive theme settings, palettes (supported preset names), home_url , theme_script , logo_url , favicon_url , extra_stylesheets , and framework_stylesheet (null for none ). Load the optional framework CSS before stylesheet . The page object includes its API identifier and kind , both null for authored pages, as well as all front matter settings. Symbol kinds are also in symbols.json . Explicitly enabled plugins are loaded from the doukimd.plugins Python entry-point group. Each entry point exposes an object with a @doukimd.plugins.hookimpl method named doukimd_context(config) returning a JSON-compatible mapping. Its values appear under plugins.<plugin-name> . Configuration order defines invocation order. Missing plugins, unsupported hooks, and invalid results fail the build. Plugins run trusted Python code. Initial boundaries Arx collection, inherited members, dynamic Python APIs, automatic repository source links, incremental builds, a preview server, and cross-project inventories are follow-up work. Arx configuration is rejected until an adapter can consume retained frontend docstrings.

Images and Markdown image attachments are embedded as data URLs, with SVG kept in image context. HTML outputs use sandboxed frames with scripts, forms, parent access, and external resource loading disabled. Inline styles and embedded data images are allowed; frames can be resized vertically. Interactive widgets and JavaScript outputs are not executed. Rich-output links are separate from document reference validation. Try doukimd build --config examples/notebooks/doukimd.yaml for a complete example with saved output.
title: Authoring and configuration · Notebooks

text: Local search Search is enabled by default and runs in the reader's browser, using only the bundled search.js and lazily fetched search.json . It indexes guide prose, code, generated API documentation, and visible notebook content, with links to Markdown heading anchors. API result titles include qualified identities. Each query requires all its words; title matches rank above body matches, and results keep the best matching section per page. search: enabled: true limit: 8 min_length: 2 limit accepts 1–50 results; min_length accepts 1–10 characters. Set search: false in page front matter or notebook page metadata to omit that page from the index. This affects search, not whether the page is published. Disabling the site search omits its controls, script, and index. Open search with the header button, / , or Ctrl/Cmd+K when outside editable controls. Arrow keys move between results, Tab follows native dialog focus, and Escape closes the dialog and restores focus. Queries support Unicode normalization and case-insensitive matching. Failed index loads show a retry message. Result text is inserted as text, never interpreted as HTML. Serve the generated site over HTTP, including under a repository subpath. For local use: python -m http.server --directory build . Browsers generally block fetching the search index when opening HTML through file:// . Search requires JavaScript and native dialog support; other navigation works without either. Custom themes receive search , search_script , and search_index_url to integrate their own controls. The index is a JSON array of {title, url, text} records, with site-root-relative page and section URLs.
title: Authoring and configuration · Local search

text: Themes and plugins The bundled theme uses Bootstrap by default. Configure presentation under theme : theme: framework: bootstrap color_mode: auto palette: terracotta framework accepts bootstrap or none ; the latter omits Bootstrap for custom themes. Bootstrap 5.3.8 CSS and its license are bundled locally. Builds and readers do not need a CDN, npm, or Bootstrap JavaScript. The built-in layout and appearance controls also work with none . color_mode accepts auto (the system preference), light , or dark . Readers can change Appearance in the header; their choice overrides the configured default and is saved per project when browser storage is available. System mode follows subsequent OS preference changes. Without JavaScript, the configured light/dark mode is used; auto falls back to light. Navigation stays usable without JavaScript, including on mobile. palette accepts five presets: terracotta (the default), ocean , forest , violet , and slate . Each has light and dark colors and works with either framework setting. Readers can change Palette in the header independently of Appearance; both choices persist per project when storage is available. Invalid saved values fall back to configuration. Without JavaScript, the configured palette still applies. Light and dark colors for all five presets Select the chart to open it at full size. It shows all nine theme color roles in both modes, using the exact preset values. Terracotta keeps DoukiMD's original colors. The other four presets use Radix Colors 3.0.0 scales under the MIT license, bundled with their attribution. They require no Radix components, npm package, or network access. Body text, muted text, links, and active navigation colors are checked at 4.5:1 or better against their backgrounds. API-kind colors stay consistent across palettes. API labels identify modules, classes, functions, and methods in navigation and declaration headings. Method kinds are collected from class parentage, including static and class methods. Labels use text as well as color. Set theme.directory to a local directory containing page.html to override the bundled HTML template. Themes receive the content context plus content , navigation (the selected sidebar), navbar , sidebar_title , table_of_contents , and stylesheet . Navigation entries expose title , relative url , kind (null for authored pages), current (exact route), active (current route or descendant), and recursive children . Group-only entries have a null url ; render their labels without an anchor. Table-of-contents entries expose title , anchor url , and level ( h2 or h3 ). Both structures are planned by the engine and can be styled by themes. HTML autoescaping is enabled; only the engine-rendered content should use Jinja's safe filter. Templates also receive theme settings, palettes (supported preset names), home_url , theme_script , logo_url , favicon_url , extra_stylesheets , and framework_stylesheet (null for none ). Load the optional framework CSS before stylesheet . The page object includes its API identifier and kind , both null for authored pages, as well as all front matter settings. Symbol kinds are also in symbols.json . Explicitly enabled plugins are loaded from the doukimd.plugins Python entry-point group. Each entry point exposes an object with a @doukimd.plugins.hookimpl method named doukimd_context(config) returning a JSON-compatible mapping. Its values appear under plugins.<plugin-name> . Configuration order defines invocation order. Missing plugins, unsupported hooks, and invalid results fail the build. Plugins run trusted Python code.
